group.passage: On the battlefield, soldiers not only need to be equipped with high-quality weapons but also require defensive armor to shield themselves from enemy’s attack. The muscle cuirass was a type of armor in ancient times designed to fit the wearer’s core part of the body and mimic an idealized male figure. Its design, imitating the human body, was inspired by the concept of heroic nude in Greek art. Originating in late Archaic Greece, the muscle cuirass became widespread in the 5th and 4th centuries BCE. The earliest known depiction of such gear dates back to around 470-460 BCE on a sculptural warrior’s upper body on the fort of Athens. Although the Greek historian, Polybius, didn’t mention muscle cuirass in his description of the types of Roman armor, archaeological evidence suggests that it was worn in combats. The combat suit was made in two pieces, the front and the back, then hammered together, weighing around 25 pounds. Initially made of bronze, it was later crafted from molded leather so that the bulky outfit became much lighter for quick moves. Muscle cuirasses are frequently portrayed in Greek and Roman art, worn by generals, emperors, and gods. Roman sculptures often feature highly decorated and delicate muscle cuirasses with mythological scenes. In contrast, simpler versions of the armor were worn by the soldiers on the battlefield, most of whom were officers or commanders. There were various types of the Roman officers’ protective equipment, with decorative leather at the armholes and lower edges serving as “uniforms” to distinguish senior officers. Unlike in ancient Greece, the muscle cuirass in the Roman Empire was a symbol of wealth and status, and its value lay in its capacity to impress. During the later stage of the Roman empire, various types of armor more suitable for combat were already widespread, but only the muscle cuirass, ornamented with fancy designs, could showcase the extraordinary status of its wearer. For example, Roman emperors in sculptures frequently wore highly embellished muscle cuirasses, symbolizing their mastery over the world, with elaborate decorations unique to Roman cuirasses and not found on Greek ones.

figures.label: 第1題選項 (A)–(D)
figures.caption: 第1題選項 (A)–(D)：四幅身穿不同盔甲的人物黑白插圖
figures.description: 四個選項各是一幅黑白線稿人物插圖（上半身至大腿），由左至右排列：(A) 中世紀騎士：頭戴罩住頭頸的鎖子甲兜帽，身穿及膝的寬鬆長罩袍，腰繫有圓形金屬扣飾的皮帶，戴手套的一手扶著一面繪有十字紋章的盾牌；軀幹沒有塑出肌肉線條的胸甲。(B) 現代奇幻風格造型的男子：高領圍巾遮住口鼻，一側肩膀與上臂覆蓋分節的護肩、臂甲並斜掛過胸前，裡面是無袖上衣；不是貼合整個軀幹的胸甲。(C) 古希臘／羅馬式戰士：頭戴頭盔，身穿貼合軀幹、雕塑出胸肌與腹肌線條的胸甲，胸甲下緣垂著一排長條皮革（裙甲），手邊可見一把短劍。(D) 古代中國兵士（兵馬俑造型）：頭戴冠帽，身穿由許多小方形甲片編綴而成的甲衣，手持長矛。

questions.stem: Which of the following pictures best illustrates the image of the muscle cuirass?

options.A: ［圖］中世紀騎士：頭戴鎖子甲兜帽，身穿及膝寬鬆長罩袍，腰繫皮帶，手扶繪有十字紋章的盾牌；沒有塑出肌肉線條的胸甲。
options.B: ［圖］高領圍巾遮住口鼻的男子，一側肩膀與上臂覆蓋分節護肩、臂甲並斜掛過胸前，裡面穿無袖上衣。
options.C: ［圖］頭戴頭盔的古希臘／羅馬式戰士，身穿雕塑出胸肌與腹肌線條、貼合軀幹的胸甲，下緣垂著一排長條皮革（裙甲）。
options.D: ［圖］兵馬俑造型的古代中國兵士，頭戴冠帽，身穿由許多小方形甲片編綴而成的甲衣，手持長矛。
